societies.name: Miracleman — Olympus-era Earth
societies.society: The established free-provision order under Miracleman and his allies

scope.continuity: Olympus and Golden Age comic story arcs
scope.period: The implemented utopian order after the London catastrophe
scope.population: Living human residents of the transformed Earth
exclusions: Every requested cure as automatically granted
Resurrected artificial bodies as a measured additional human population
An ordinary democratic mandate inferred from public approval

societies.description:
Miracleman and his allies replace the old economy with a technologically transformed Earth where money is abolished and goods are free. Warpsmith and Qys capabilities help reshape material conditions, while abundant sustainable energy and restored fertile land support ordinary life. The guarantee estimate is strong for that implemented order. It is qualified by the rulers’ discretion: the later Golden Age includes a refusal to help a father’s brain-damaged daughter, so universal fulfillment of every personal need would overstate the evidence.

Control remains concentrated in the superhuman leadership and its alien collaborators. This is a disclosed analogy to the concentrated non-AI position, not a claim that alien or enhanced biological rulers are machines. Popular approval does not establish equal ownership or a right to overrule Olympus. Useful art, care, research and public services can continue even without money. The story summary supplies no all-person work census, so nonworking remains unresolved rather than treating universal free goods as universal idleness.

guarantees.basis: The implemented Olympus order explicitly abolishes money, supplies free goods and transforms productive energy/ecology through advanced allied technology.

control.basis: Superhuman and alien biological rulers concentrate authority; 0 is an explicit non-AI elite analogy.

nonworking.basis: Free goods and abolished currency do not census useful chosen labor.

societies.name: Transmetropolitan — The City’s unequal Maker economy
societies.society: Household fabrication amid continued class exclusion

scope.continuity: Original comic, issue 2 Maker column and related City depictions
scope.period: Established City life during Spider Jerusalem’s reporting
scope.population: Living humans and human-derived City residents
exclusions: Every citizen as owning a Maker
People revived into neglect as guaranteed secure housing

societies.description:
Makers can fabricate meals, clothing and other goods within an ordinary household. The comic’s own column explains that middle-class families can afford a machine while its ideal feedstock is far more expensive; garbage converters offer a less efficient substitute. Families without Makers continue buying packaged necessities, and competition for reusable refuse exposes the class divide. This is actual automatic material production with uneven access, rather than a purely theoretical invention.

Guarantees are weak because neither the machine nor its inputs are universally supplied, and the broader City continues to neglect vulnerable residents. Household possession disperses some productive capacity, but ownership of the relevant infrastructure and inputs is not established as equally shared; control remains unresolved instead of reading private appliances as a democratic commons. Human-derived residents remain visible despite changes of body. Journalism, fabrication design, cleaning, care and other useful work continue, while deprivation is not a nonworking statistic. The point describes the unequal implemented economy and does not duplicate it as a separate zero variant solely because access is restricted.

guarantees.basis: Issue 2 explicitly describes actual household material fabrication and costly inputs; people without machines remain dependent on purchases.

control.basis: Personal Maker ownership is widespread in one class, but effective control of productive infrastructure and input supplies remains unresolved.

nonworking.basis: Neither Maker ownership nor poverty supplies an all-person useful-work census.

evidence.claim: Issue 2 explicitly describes actual household material fabrication and costly inputs; people without machines remain dependent on purchases.
evidence.locator: Bounded named-society economic and story sections

review_notes: Twelve sequential short-reference dispositions, two retained records. Unclear superhero economies were not rescued by reading long continuity histories.
Miracleman’s alien/superhuman rulers use an explicit concentrated non-AI analogy; discretionary medical refusal qualifies guarantees.
Transmetropolitan is supported by a bounded indexed primary Maker column reproduced in analysis, not merely by fan speculation about replicators. No PDF retrieval or render.
Red Son’s no-unemployment statement is not converted to nonworking; surgically altered humans remain human-derived workers.
Unrelated musical-authority, Krypton engineering-company and academic nanotechnology results were discarded.
